A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GCSE research despite the changed title and presentation. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including distinguishing retained experiments from additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original GCSE experiments on STS, reranking, and transfer tasks, plus ablations, case studies, and ChatGLM-3 LoRA results.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results, expanded LLM experiments, and new diversity, gradient, error, and filtering-threshold analyses.

M1.justification: Equations 12–13 change the hard-negative denominator term from G to exp(G) and make Gaussian attenuation conditional on s_i <= s'_i, using G = s_i otherwise. Appendix A also changes generation operations: preceding-text generation becomes summarization, and knowledge-JSON rewriting becomes masked-word completion. These materially revise the stated loss and synthesis procedure, although the main-text prompt description is not fully reconciled.

E1.justification: v1 uses NLI plus STS-Benchmark and SICK for training and synthesis. v3 adds a Wikipedia-based default setting and reports STS-12, PAWS, and SICK as the domain-training sources in its second setting. This substantially changes training-data coverage. The seven STS benchmarks, four reranking datasets, and seven transfer tasks remain.

E2.justification: The main STS, reranking, and transfer comparator sets are retained; ChatGPT is relabeled GPT-3.5 Turbo with matching baseline scores. The supplementary LLM comparison changes: v1 Table 9's SimCSE, Flan-T5-XL, and ChatGPT comparison entries disappear, while v3 Table 10 compares unsupervised LoRA controls against augmented training.

E3.justification: v3 expands synthesis from ChatGLM3-6B to five LLM configurations and introduces paired unsupervised-versus-augmented training across five decoder models. New analysis protocols include 5,000-source-sample t-SNE, initial-versus-step-125 gradient comparisons, controlled filtering-threshold sweeps, and normalized prediction errors exceeding 0.2 for FP/FN counts. The existing STS and reranking metrics and default filtering/temperature/decay hyperparameters remain.

E4.justification: v3 adds FP/FN error analysis (Figure 1), synthetic-sample diversity analysis (Appendix C), prediction and gradient diagnostics (Appendix H), filtering-threshold sensitivity (Appendix I), and direct augmentation controls for LLM embeddings (Appendix G). These substantially expand the evidence about diversity, denoising, and applicability. The earlier component, domain-ratio, sigma, and SynCSE ablations and five case studies are retained.

E5.justification: v3 Table 2 newly reports t-test significance against comparable baselines at p < 0.5%, and Figure 1 displays error bars absent from v1. Run counts, seeds, the meaning of the bars, and the test's replication unit are not specified. These are reporting additions, without evidence establishing additional repeated runs.

E6.justification: STS and transfer results are extensively revised and expanded. BERT-base GCSE averages 81.21 in v1 Table 1; v3 reports 81.61 for the Wikipedia setting and 81.35 for its revised domain setting, so these are not matched-setting gains. The domain ablation's no-decay average changes from 80.83 to 81.09. v3 also adds multiple-generator and paired LoRA results. Reranking, entity-awareness, five-case-study, and SynCSE-ablation numbers are retained.

T1.justification: The KG definitions, entity-search equations, and basic contrastive formulation remain. v3 makes localized substantive revisions to the loss definitions in Equations 12–13 and adds Appendix J's clipped normalization anchored to median predictions at the minimum and maximum gold labels, with an outlier-resistance rationale. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both retain knowledge-based entity/quantity augmentation, Gaussian denoising, and efficient STS performance as their core contributions. v3 adds explicit priority claims for combining KGs with LLM sample synthesis and extends reported STS superiority to all four backbones; v1's detailed results acknowledge a RoBERTa-base exception.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations about knowledge-generated samples filling sparse semantic regions, filtering thresholds balancing sample availability against noise, and augmentation improving decoder-based sentence embeddings. Its new Limitations section attributes differences across LLM sizes to prompt adherence and alignment. These substantially expand applicability and failure-condition discussion beyond v1, while retaining the earlier domain-ratio and sigma interpretations.

D1.justification: v3 adds a paper-specific code-availability link, an A800 80GB synthesis GPU disclosure, and eight TITAN RTX GPUs for training and validation. Appendix A substantially revises the supplied prompt templates and JSON schemas and includes worked examples. Appendix G documents last-position hidden-state extraction and Pretended CoT for the LoRA studies. v1 supplied prompts and core hyperparameters but lacked these access and implementation disclosures.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused positioning against SynCSE and MultiCSR through Table 1's knowledge and denoising distinctions, a locally weighted learning motivation, and discussion of works including GS-InfoNCE, AoE, BeLLM, and domain-adapted embeddings. The earlier RAG discussion and Mitra/Ryu citations are removed. The principal contrastive sentence-embedding research context remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are extensively rewritten around low diversity and high noise. Four method subsections become two grouped subsections, reranking moves into Appendix B, the appendices are reorganized, and Limitations and Ethics sections are added. Author and header text also changes.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column document with substantially resized and relocated displays. v3 adds an overall workflow, method-comparison and low-resource results tables, and error, diversity, gradient, and threshold plots. The prompt table becomes Figures 8–9, while STS and transfer tables expand to distinguish synthesis LLMs.

improvement.justification: The new gradient and threshold diagnostics, broader generator comparisons, and paired augmentation controls improve support for the mechanism and applicability claims; code and hardware disclosures also help reproducibility. The gain is limited by underspecified statistical procedures and new inconsistencies. Section 3.1's prompt descriptions disagree with Figures 8–9, and Appendix D claims GPT-3.5 leads all transfer backbones although Table 7 reports BERT-large averages of 88.29 for GPT-3.5 versus 88.88 for GLM4.
